battle.name: 廬州之戰
battle.brief: 宋嘉熙二年（1238）十一月，蒙古軍進攻淮西重鎮廬州，宋淮西兵與荊襄兵合勢赴援。趙葵督中軍扼城，孟珙遣精兵夜襲蒙古營寨、焚其積聚，大軍乘亂出城夾擊，蒙古軍退走十餘里，宋軍追奔數十里。城頭與追擊途中，宋軍以神臂弓、蹶張弩齊射壓制蒙古騎兵，弩機張弦雖慢，仍是遠射的骨幹。

kit.name: 十字弩
kit.history: 弩把射速交給了機械，代價是裝填慢。城牆上它比長弓可靠，野戰裡它比長弓脆弱。

countries: 這場戰爭是蒙古大汗國對南宋的一次戰役，發生在宋嘉熙二年（1238）蒙古戊戌年冬季，地點在淮西路的廬州，即今安徽合肥。蒙古一方由窩闊台汗統轄的東路、中路大軍擔任，兵馬自河南、蔡州一帶南下，沿汴河與淮河水系推進，兵眾以數萬計，並在州城郊野築壘列營、備辦攻城器械；其指揮體系仍循蒙古十戶、百戶、千戶、萬戶的編制，諸王與萬戶各領一軍。蒙古新得的北方漢地州縣為其供應糧秣、攻城器物與工匠，漢地軍戶亦被編入隊伍。南宋一方則以淮西制置趙葵所領的淮西兵為中軍，荊襄兵馬都統制孟珙所部由襄陽、鄂州方向兼程趕來策應，州城守軍由守臣與州兵、禁軍、弓箭手、弩手組成，另有滁州方向杜杲所部與盱眙方向各路宋軍彼此聲援。整條江淮戰線同時在安豐、滁州、壽春多處受攻，廬州之戰是其中最見成敗的一次。宋方以城垣為依托、以弩弓壓制騎兵，逐漸摸出對付蒙古機動兵團的守城反擊路子；蒙古則以圍城打援、游騎斷糧的辦法，企圖把宋軍拖入消耗戰。
countriesEn: This war was a campaign of the Mongol empire against the Southern Song, fought in the winter of the second year of the Jiaxi era, 1238, in the prefecture of Luzhou in the circuit of West Huai, modern Hefei in Anhui. On the Mongol side stood the eastern and central columns of the army under the Great Khan Ogedei, tens of thousands of men who had come south through Henan and the region of Caizhou, moving along the Bian river and the waterways of the Huai, who dug in on the open ground outside the prefectural city, ringed their camp with a timber palisade and brought up siege engines; their chain of command still followed the Mongol decimal organisation of ten-, hundred-, thousand- and ten-thousand-household units, with princes and meliks each commanding a division. The Han Chinese prefectures newly taken in the north supplied the Mongols with grain, siege materials and craftsmen, and Han households were enrolled into the units. On the Song side, the middle army was the army of West Huai under Zhao Kui, who held the office of Pacification Commissioner for that circuit; Meng Gong, Commander of the Jingxiang armies, marched in to support him from the Xiangyang and Ezhou direction, while the city itself was held by the prefectural garrison, the imperial guard units and the foot archers and crossbowmen of the prefecture; other Song forces at Chuzhou under Du Gao and in the Xuyi direction supported the line in mutual cooperation. The whole Jianghuai front was under attack at the same time at Anfeng, Chuzhou and Shouchun, and the battle of Luzhou was the one of these that produced a clear result. The Song built their defence on the city walls and used the crossbow and the bow to hold the Mongol horse at bay, gradually working out a way to defend a city and counter-attack against a mobile steppe army; the Mongols answered with the siege-and-intercept method and with raiding parties that cut the supply road, hoping to drag the Song army into a war of attrition.
people: 宋方統帥是趙葵。他是宋宗室，以淮西制置兼領中軍，此役中他表現出的長處是持重：蒙古軍逼近州城，他不貿然出城決戰，先問計於孟珙。孟珙是這場戰役真正的主謀。他以荊襄兵馬都統制的身份率兵北上，提出敵眾我寡、糧道不繼，不可與之久持，主張以精兵夜襲蒙古營寨、焚燒其所掠糧草，使敵人無法就地補充，再由大軍乘亂出城夾擊。《宋史·孟珙傳》所記夜襲的執行者，是孟珙分遣的將佐，其中點名的有宋武；同傳另記珙事先分兵、張弓弩以待，設伏於敵營之側。州城守成的部分，由合肥守臣與城中將佐主持，姓名在傳世記載中不詳。蒙古方面的最高決策者是窩闊台汗，是他在位期間決定全面南侵；耶律楚材曾在1237年末至1238年間從征河南時力言南征非宜，請以河朔借糧為議，兩度進諫止戰，窩闊台不從，遂有1238年冬季的兩淮之役。蒙古統兵的主將姓名在《元史·太宗本紀》與《宋史》各篇所記互有出入，只能確定此軍隸屬蒙古對宋作戰的東路、中路大軍，諸王與萬戶分領其眾。同一條江淮戰線上的滁州由杜杲守城應敵，與廬州互為犄角；杜杲後來在採石之戰中以木製霹靂砲破敵，被視為南方火器與守城術的代表人物。
peopleEn: The Song commander was Zhao Kui, a member of the imperial clan who held the office of Pacification Commissioner for West Huai and led the middle army. What he showed in this campaign was caution: with the Mongol army pressing close to the city he did not rush out to give battle, but asked Meng Gong for advice first. Meng Gong was the real author of the victory. Marching north with the Jingxiang armies under his command as Commander of those forces, he argued that the enemy was numerous and their supply line was short, that no long war of attrition could be fought, and proposed to send picked troops out at night to fall on the Mongol camp and burn the grain and supplies the enemy had seized, so that the Mongols could not refit on the spot, and then to bring the main army out of the city to strike them while they were disordered. The Song History biography of Meng Gong names the men who carried out the night attack as officers he detailed for the task, and Song Wu is among those named; the same biography also records that Meng Gong had divided his troops in advance, strung out his bows and crossbows, and posted them in ambush on the flank of the enemy camp. The holding of the city was in the hands of the prefect of Hefei and the officers of the garrison, whose names are not preserved in the transmitted records. On the Mongol side the supreme decision was Ogedei Khan's, who was ruling when the general invasion of the Song was launched; Yelü Chucai had argued during the campaigning in Henan in late 1237 and in 1238 that the southern expedition was ill-advised, proposed to settle the matter by borrowing grain from the northern districts instead, and petitioned twice to halt the war, but Ogedei would not listen, and the winter campaign of 1238 in the two Huai followed. The name of the Mongol general in the field differs between the Yuan History chronicle of Taizong and the various biographies of the Song History; what can be fixed is that this force belonged to the eastern and central columns of the Mongol war against the Song, with princes and meliks commanding parts of it. At Chuzhou on the same Jianghuai front Du Gao held the city against the enemy, and Chuzhou and Luzhou supported one another; Du Gao later broke the enemy at the battle of Caishi with a wooden thunder-stone catapult, and is remembered as a representative of southern gunnery and siegecraft.
kits: 卡面這件十字弩是歐洲的形制：弩臂、弦、機括與望山構成一組，張弦靠人力絞轉的螺杆或蹶臂固定進弩匣，扣下機括即能放矢，射速由機構決定，遠勝手開的長弓。十字弩在歐洲興起於11世紀末，與卡面標出的年代相合。但這場戰役發生在中國，歐式弩具並不在廬州城下的戰場上：宋代中國自有源遠流長的弩，漢唐以來即是軍隊標配，宋人不會捨手邊的熟器而取歐式形制。宋軍此役真正倚重的，是大型臂弩神臂弓與步卒所用的蹶張弩、步弩。神臂弓以木為弩身，《宋史·兵志》記其弩弦需三壯士合力張開，雖射不入石亦能及三百步，所用箭矢能貫榆柳之木；《武經總要》所繪的形制則更誇張，弩臂長三尺二寸、矢長三尺五寸，射程可及三百四十步。蹶張弩則以腳蹬槓桿張弦，射手可伏地而射，士卒便能一面跪伏、一面完成裝填。弩的代價正是卡面那句話：裝填慢。守城時有城牆、有女牆、有時間，弩手只需在敵騎逼近的數十步內把箭送出去，一輪齊射的壓力足以擋住蒙古騎兵的第一次衝鋒；但在開闊的野地上，蒙古騎兵轉瞬即逝，弩手裝填的間隙就是敵人穿過的窗口，因此宋軍野戰仍以長弓、刀槍與騎兵相配合。蒙古軍隊的裝備與此形成對照：他們以蒙古弓射擊，進攻時用拋石機（西域所傳的回回砲）、撞竿、雲梯與穴地，圍城時壘木為柵、掘壕為障，並倚仗騎兵游弋去斷宋軍的糧道；步卒對步卒的近戰仍靠長槍、刀與蒙皮盾。雙方運輸以牛馬車隊、輜重與河運糧船維持。
kitsEn: The crossbow on the card is the European form: a prod, a string, a trigger mechanism and a sighting device make up the assembly, the string is drawn by a screw-turned windlass or a crane lever and locked into the stock, and the release of the mechanism sends the bolt, with the rate of fire decided by the mechanism rather than by the arm. The crossbow spread across Europe at the end of the eleventh century, which matches the date on the card. But this campaign was fought in China, and no European crossbow stood on the field below the walls of Luzhou: China had its own long tradition of the crossbow, a standard weapon of the army from the Han and Tang dynasties onward, and the Song had no reason to abandon the serviceable tool at hand in favour of a European pattern. What the Song army actually relied on here was the large power crossbow, the shenbi gong, together with the juezhang crossbow and the ordinary foot crossbows used by the infantry. The shenbi gong had a wooden body; the Song History records that its string required three strong men to draw it, that it would carry three hundred paces even though it could not shoot into stone, and that its bolts could pierce elm and willow wood, while the forms drawn in the Wujing Zongyao are grander still, with a prod three chi and two cun long, bolts of three chi and five cun and a range of three hundred and forty paces. The juezhang crossbow was drawn by a foot lever, so the archer could lie down to shoot and complete the loading on his knees. The price of the crossbow is exactly what the card says: slow loading. In defence, with walls, parapets and time on their side, the crossbowman only had to put the bolt away in the few dozen paces before the enemy horse arrived, and the pressure of a single volley was enough to break the first charge of the Mongol horse; but on open ground the Mongol horse was gone in an instant, and the interval needed for reloading was the window through which the enemy passed, so in the field the Song still relied on the long bow, on spear and blade, and on their own cavalry. The Mongol equipment made the opposite impression: they shot with the Mongol bow, brought up catapults (the huihui pao transmitted from the western regions), battering rams, scaling ladders and sapping to the walls, ringed their camps with a timber palisade and dug a ditch around them, and relied on roving horse parties to cut the Song supply road; for close combat between foot and foot they still used the long spear, the blade and rawhide shields. On both sides the movement of everything was kept up by ox and horse teams, baggage trains and grain boats on the waterways.
tactics: 蒙古軍的攻城部署是蒙古人的老辦法：先以大隊騎兵抵近州城，選擇城北與城西的平曠築營壘，壘木為柵、掘壕為圍，把營區變成一座可以進攻的野城；再分出以千騎為一組的游騎四出，既偵察宋軍援兵的方向，也兼做劫掠，把廬州周邊村舍的糧秣往營中搬，試圖在援軍到齊之前先耗盡宋軍。攻城本身用拋石機壓制城頭、穴地近壕、撞竿撞門、雲梯臨城，而蒙古人特別習慣圍城打援：一面留兵繼續進攻，另一面在半路截擊來援的宋軍，廬州與滁州同時受攻，正是這種打法。宋軍這邊，趙葵的淮西兵以城垣為核心，弓弩手分列城頭與女牆，遠者用神臂弓壓制城下之敵，近者用蹶張弩齊射；孟珙的荊襄兵不急著列陣硬撼，而是先在州城與營壘之間相機而動，待蒙古軍夜中宿營、馬未卸鞍之際，遣精兵銜枚夜出，直插敵營，以火焚其帳幕、柴草與劫掠所得的糧秣，隨即回身，與城內出擊的主力夾擊一處。蒙軍遭焚，營中火光與驚呼同時而起，騎兵在黑暗中無法展開衝鋒，隊形一亂便直潰；宋軍乘勝追奔數十里，直到敵騎脫離接戰才收兵。追擊途中宋軍仍以弩箭齊射收束敵陣——這正是弩最合適的位置：不必與騎兵比速度，只在它衝過來的那幾十步內打它。
tacticsEn: The Mongol deployment for the siege followed the old Mongol pattern. A large body of horse came up close to the prefectural city, chose the open ground to the north and west of it to build a camp, piled timber into a palisade and dug a ditch around it, and turned the camp into a field fortress from which the attack could be made; then they detached roving parties of a thousand horse at a time to range in all directions, partly to scout the direction from which Song reinforcements would come, partly to raid, carrying grain and provisions out of the villages around Luzhou into the camp, in the hope of wearing the Song army out before its relief could arrive. The siege itself was worked with catapults to silence the parapets, sapping to approach the ditch, battering rams against the gates and scaling ladders brought up to the walls, and the Mongols were particularly given to the method of besieging one city while intercepting the relief force: they left troops to keep up the pressure and sent others to meet the Song army coming to the rescue halfway. Luzhou and Chuzhou being attacked at the same time was precisely that method at work. On the Song side, Zhao Kui's West Huai army made the city walls the core of its position, with archers and crossbowmen posted along the parapets and the wall-head, the power crossbows used at range against the enemy below the walls and the juezhang crossbows used for massed volleys at close distance. Meng Gong's Jingxiang troops did not hurry to array themselves for a head-on clash; they first watched for the moment between the city and the Mongol camp, and when the Mongol army lay encamped at night with its horses unsaddled he sent picked troops out with their mouths stopped, straight into the enemy camp, to set fire to the tents, the brushwood and the grain that had been plundered, and then wheeled back to strike from the other side together with the main force sallied out from the city. The camp was burning, fire and shouting rose at once, the horse could not form up in the dark, and the line came apart; the Song followed up the victory for several tens of li, breaking off only when the enemy horse had shaken them off. During the pursuit the Song still used massed crossbow bolts to gather the fleeing enemy into a manageable body, and this was the one place the crossbow belonged: it did not have to race the horse, it only had to shoot it in the few dozen paces through which it charged.
data: 有根據可寫的數字大致如下。時間是宋嘉熙二年（1238）十一月，即蒙古戊戌年冬季；蒙古軍自河南方向南下，人數以數萬計，其統兵主將的姓名在傳世記載中互見歧異。進攻位置，《宋史·孟珙傳》稱蒙古軍逼近廬州州城數十里，並在州郊結營。宋軍方面，趙葵領淮西兵為中軍，孟珙率荊襄兵自鄂州北上策應，兩軍合兵；夜襲的支隊規模，史料只作精兵、精騎而未給出確數，故此處不列具體人數。戰果方面，本傳記載宋軍追奔數十里、斬獲甚眾，俘虜數百、奪馬數千匹，數目屬概略的概數，不宜當作精確統計。廬州城沿用隋唐以來合肥舊城改建，垣周約二十餘里，環巢湖，控淝水、廬江與淮河之間的水陸轉運，是淮西軍的糧秣樞紐。器械方面可引的具體數字在弩上：《武經總要》所記神臂弓弩臂長三尺二寸、矢長三尺五寸、射程約三百四十步，《宋史·兵志》則記其張弦需三壯士之力、雖射不入石亦能及三百步、矢能貫榆柳木，兩書所錄形制數字本有出入，引用時不宜混為一談；蹶張弩以腳蹬張弦，一次齊射的覆蓋面取決於射手數目。距離上，廬州距南宋首都臨安直線約六百五十里，荊襄兵北上須穿過江淮與淮南的縱深，糧秣靠河運與人力轉運，這正是孟珙堅持速戰速決、不與蒙軍久持的現實理由。戰役之後，孟珙在1239年得以率軍北上，收復襄陽、隨州、壽昌三處失地，荊襄一線的戰局由此翻轉。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. The time was the eleventh month of the second year of Jiaxi, 1238, that is the winter of the Mongol year Wuxu; the Mongol army came south through Henan and numbered on the order of tens of thousands, while the name of the commander in the field differs between the transmitted records. As to the position of the attack, the Song History biography of Meng Gong states that the Mongol army closed to within several tens of li of the city of Luzhou and encamped in the open outside it. On the Song side, Zhao Kui led the West Huai army as the middle army and Meng Gong brought the Jingxiang troops north from Ezhou to support him, the two forces joining hands. The size of the night-attack detachment is given in the source only as picked troops and picked horse, without a definite number, so no headcount is offered here. As for results, the same biography records that the Song pursued for several tens of li and took heavy toll, with several hundred prisoners taken and several thousand horses captured; these are rough approximations and should not be read as exact statistics. The city of Luzhou had been rebuilt on the old Hefei site of the Sui and Tang and its circuit ran a little over twenty li; it ringed Chaohu lake and commanded the water and land routes between the Fei river, the Lujiang and the Huai, and it was the hinge of grain and provisions for the West Huai army. The figures that can be quoted for equipment belong to the crossbow: the Wujing Zongyao gives the shenbi gong a prod three chi and two cun long, bolts of three chi and five cun and a range of about three hundred and forty paces, while the Song History records that its string needed three strong men to draw it, that it still reached three hundred paces although it could not shoot into stone, and that its bolts could pierce elm and willow; the two books differ in the dimensions they give, and the two sets of figures should not be run together. The juezhang crossbow was drawn by the foot, and the ground covered by a single volley depended on the number of archers. As for distance, the straight line from Luzhou to the Song capital Lin'an is about six hundred and fifty li, and the Jingxiang troops marching north had to cross the depth of Jianghuai and the lands south of the Huai, with grain moved by river boat and by human porterage, which was the practical reason behind Meng Gong's insistence on striking quickly rather than enduring a long war against the Mongols. After the campaign Meng Gong was able to march north in 1239 and recover Xiangyang, Suizhou and Shouchang, and the line in Jingxiang turned over as a result.
cause: 直接原因是蒙古在北方得手之後，需要向南方取得補給。窩闊台汗在位時，金朝已亡於1234年，河北、山東、河南的漢地雖已歸附蒙古，卻缺乏足夠的馬匹、軍需與攻城器械來支撐新的大戰；同時蒙古的兵勢正處於西征歸來的轉折點，南方的糧食、船舶與工料成了最現成的補充來源。1236年起，蒙古分路大舉南侵：西路由闊端指向蜀地，中路與東路取河南、趨兩淮，兵鋒直指江淮走廊。廬州是淮西的軍府與糧秣中轉之地，環巢湖、扼淝水與淮河間的漕運，又有合肥一線的倉儲，蒙古若要打通淮南、迫近采石與兩浙，就必須先拿下此地。同一條戰線上，蒙古還在安豐、滁州、壽春等處同時用兵，分散了宋廷的應援力量，企圖以多點施壓逼宋廷顧此失彼。蒙古內部對是否南征並非一致，耶律楚材主張以河朔借粟議和，認為南征所得不足以抵償民怨與兵禍，兩度進諫，窩闊台不聽，遂有1238年冬季的兩淮之役。宋廷此刻正處於紹興以來最被動的局面：邊防線被壓到江淮，重慶、襄陽等上游要地已失，淮西雖有趙葵、孟珙等宿將，但兵員與糧秣都吃緊，於是有了這場以守待援、伺隙反擊的廬州之戰。
causeEn: The immediate cause was that the Mongols, having won in the north, needed to draw supplies from the south. Under Ogedei Khan, the Jin dynasty had already fallen in 1234, and although the Han Chinese lands of Hebei, Shandong and Henan had submitted to the Mongols, they did not provide the horses, war material and siege engines needed to support a new great campaign; the Mongol military was also at a turning point after the western expeditions, and the grain, the shipping and the craftsmen of the south were the most readily available supplement. From 1236 the Mongols advanced south in several columns: the western column under Koden aimed at Shu, the middle and eastern columns took Henan and drove towards the two Huai, with the point of their spears directed at the Jianghuai corridor. Luzhou was the military headquarters and the transhipment point of West Huai, ringed by Chaohu lake and holding the waterways of the Fei and the Huai, with the granaries of the Hefei line behind it; if the Mongols were to open the route south of the Huai and press towards Caishi and the Zhe region, they had to take this place first. On the same front they were also fighting at Anfeng, Chuzhou and Shouchun at the same time, spreading the Song court's capacity to respond and hoping to force it to be stretched too thin to deal with each point. The Mongol leadership was not united on the question: Yelü Chucai argued for settling things by borrowing grain from the northern districts, holding that the southern campaign could not make good either the resentment of the people or the cost of the war, and he petitioned twice; Ogedei would not listen, and so the winter campaign of 1238 in the two Huai followed. The Song court at that moment was in the most difficult position since the Shaoxing era: the frontier had been pushed back to the river, upstream strongholds such as Chongqing and Xiangyang were already lost, and although West Huai had seasoned commanders such as Zhao Kui and Meng Gong, both manpower and provisions were thin, and so there came this battle of Luzhou fought by holding the city, waiting for aid and striking at the moment the enemy showed a seam.
impact: 廬州之戰的意義不在殲滅多少蒙古兵，而在它把南宋在江淮的處境從一味挨打改成了可以局部反攻。蒙古自1211年以來攻宋，攻城略地而宋軍罕有大勝，士氣與民心都靠著蒙古不可與爭的說法撐著；此役宋軍在野戰中擊潰蒙古大軍、追奔數十里，是江淮戰線上久違的實勝，消息傳到建康與臨安，淮西各州的守臣與流民都知道了宋軍仍有還手之力。對孟珙而言，這是一個支點：正是廬州之役贏來的時間與主動權，讓他在次年得以率師北上，於1239年收復襄陽、隨州、壽昌，把被蒙古切斷的荊襄一線重新接回來，南宋的戰局第一次從守江轉為取荊。此役也示範了一套對付蒙古機動兵團的守城戰術：以城垣與弩弓拖住敵人，以精兵夜襲焚其營壘與糧秣，再用騎兵追擊其潰兵——這套經驗後來在襄陽、在採石反覆被使用。另一面，蒙古並未因此罷手，1239至1241年間雙方在兩淮、襄漢兩線仍反覆拉鋸，宋朝得到的只是一段喘息，而蒙古也從失敗中改變戰法：劉整降蒙後提出的假道於宋、迂回鄂州之策，隨即把蒙古的進攻軸線由淮西轉向長江中游，廬州的大捷並沒有改變雙方力量對比的基本走向。
impactEn: The significance of the battle of Luzhou lay less in how many Mongols were destroyed than in the fact that it changed the Song position on the Huai from a position of pure passivity into one that allowed local counter-offensive. Since 1211 the Mongols had campaigned against the Song, taking town after town, and the Song had seldom won a battle outright; morale and popular confidence were sustained by the saying that the Mongols could not be fought. This time the Song army broke a Mongol force in the open field and pursued for several tens of li, a genuine success long absent from the Huai front, and the news reaching Jiankang and Lin'an told the commanders and the displaced people of every prefecture in West Huai that the Song could still strike back. For Meng Gong it was a pivot: the time and the initiative won at Luzhou were what allowed him to march north the following year and, in 1239, recover Xiangyang, Suizhou and Shouchang, reconnecting the severed Jingxiang line; for the first time the Song war turned from holding the river to taking Jing. The campaign also demonstrated a method of defending a city against a mobile steppe army: hold the enemy with the walls, the bow and the crossbow, send picked troops out at night to burn their camp and their provisions, then let the horse pursue the routed. That combination was used again and again afterwards, at Xiangyang and at Caishi. On the other hand the Mongols did not stop: between 1239 and 1241 the two sides fought up and down the lines of the two Huai and of the Xiang-Han region, and what the Song gained was a breathing space. The Mongols also learned from their defeat and changed their method: the plan Liu Zheng proposed after defecting to them, to pass by way of the Song and turn on Ezhou, moved the Mongol axis of attack from West Huai to the middle Yangzi, and the great victory at Luzhou did not alter the basic balance between the two sides.
result: 此役的結局是蒙古軍退、宋軍追。蒙古營壘被焚、糧秣被燒，留在州郊的攻城器械與積聚大半棄置，敵騎在黑夜中失去統制，先鋒與後隊自相踐踏，趙葵與孟珙的兩軍趁勢合擊，宋軍追奔數十里，斬獲甚眾，俘虜數百、奪馬數千匹。蒙古軍退回淮北，廬州城未失，淮西的軍府與倉儲得以保全；宋廷隨即論功行賞，孟珙的荊襄兵權加重，趙葵的淮西防務也得以固定。次年1239年，孟珙乘勝收復襄陽、隨州、壽昌，荊襄與淮西兩線因此連成一體，這可以說是廬州之勝真正結出的果子。史書對本役的記載相當簡略，《宋史·孟珙傳》與《宋史·趙葵傳》各留下若干行，《元史·太宗本紀》則只記蒙古軍南下的日程，具體的戰場細節多靠這幾段本傳與時人筆記拼出來，因此兵員、斬獲、器械數目只能作概略之數。可以確定的是：這是蒙古攻宋以來宋軍在江淮取得的一次罕見的野戰勝利，也是一場以守城弩兵、夜襲焚糧與騎兵追擊配合完成的勝利；它沒有改變宋蒙長期對峙的格局，卻在1238年之後的十餘年裡，為南宋在襄漢與兩淮兩條戰線的站穩，提供了一個可以反覆援引的樣本。
resultEn: The outcome of the campaign was that the Mongol army withdrew and the Song pursued. The camp was burned, the provisions were destroyed, most of the siege engines and stores left outside the city were abandoned, the enemy horse lost its discipline in the dark, and the leading and trailing formations trampled one another. The two Song armies of Zhao Kui and Meng Gong struck together at the moment, pursued for several tens of li, took heavy toll, with several hundred prisoners and several thousand horses captured. The Mongols fell back north of the Huai; the city of Luzhou was not lost, and the military headquarters and the granaries of West Huai were preserved. The court rewarded the officers, Meng Gong's authority over the Jingxiang armies was increased, and the defence of West Huai under Zhao Kui was settled. The following year, in 1239, Meng Gong used the momentum to recover Xiangyang, Suizhou and Shouchang, so that the Jingxiang and West Huai lines were joined into one, and this is the fruit that the victory at Luzhou truly bore. The written record of the campaign is thin: the Song History biographies of Meng Gong and of Zhao Kui each preserve a few lines, while the Yuan History chronicle of Taizong records only the calendar of the Mongol advance, and the details of the field have to be pieced together from those biographies and from the notes of contemporaries, so that the figures for strength, for captures and for equipment can only be rough. What can be fixed is this: it was one of the rare open-field victories the Song had won against the Mongols since the war began, and it was won by the combination of crossbowmen on the walls, picked troops burning the enemy's provisions by night, and cavalry riding down the broken enemy. It did not change the long shape of the Song-Mongol stalemate, but for the ten years after 1238 it gave the Song a model that could be cited again and again while the Southern Song held its ground on the Xiang-Han front and along the two Huai.
